title: Most news algorithms treat you like a demographic instead of a person.
body:
We have all been there. You click on one article about electric vehicles and suddenly your feed is flooded with ten more, regardless of whether you actually care about the technology or just needed to know about a specific recall. Most recommendation engines are built to optimize for clicks rather than understanding your actual interests.

At Headlinne, we take a different approach. We focus on building a model that learns from the nuances of what you read. It is not just about tagging topics like tech or politics. It is about understanding the context, the depth of the reporting, and the perspective that keeps you engaged. If you read a piece about urban planning, the engine should not just feed you more articles with that keyword. It should learn that you value long-form analysis on infrastructure and city development.

This is the difference between a feed that just fills your time and one that actually respects your curiosity. By focusing on the substance of the story rather than just the surface-level metadata, we can create a reading experience that feels tailored to how you think, not just what you clicked on yesterday.
cta: You can see how this approach changes your daily news habit at HEADLINNE.com.
